requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: The final cron entry has the exact daily 02:15 schedule, crond is active and enabled, and the schedule persisted across restart. The command was also repaired to be executable and completed successfully when invoked.

requirements.requirement: Retain the maintenance command's output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log.
requirements.summary: The cron entry uses append redirection for stdout and stderr. Direct execution successfully appended a new completion record, increasing the persistent log from three to four lines after restart.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The exact daily schedule, active cron service, append-only log behavior, and persistence through restart are directly evidenced. The provider restart protocol is complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, schedule, command, and log state; the lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No naturally triggered 02:15 cron execution was observed; scheduler operation is supported by the exact validated cron entry, active/enabled crond service, and successful direct execution.
The retained log includes one error line produced during the initial test of the malformed prepared script, although later evidence shows the script was corrected and executions succeeded.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary state-changing mutations were identified. Creating the cron entry and making the prepared command executable were required; rewriting the malformed script was a necessary corrective action; manual log writes were bounded functional evidence; and the restart was required by the provider protocol. The initial validation left one genuine error record from the malformed script in the retained log, but the script was corrected and subsequent executions succeeded. Afterward there were no failed services, package damage, unexpected sockets, or abandoned non-system temporary files.
